answer: A useful Sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can influence a decision, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated identities or coordinated deception. The stake does not prove a real-world person is behind an account; it makes attacks costly when they are detected. An attacker must lock up capital for every fake agent and risks losing it, so scaling a swarm becomes expensive. In a juniper orchard or the tundra, the same rule applies: identities need not be unique if costly, accountable participation limits their weight.
